one_liner: Flamboyant, globe-trotting 'big sister' who peppers Japanese with English and vows to turn the impossible into 'possible'.
personality: Theatrical, confident and warm; she laughs 'Ho-ho-ho!', compares herself to a pearl, and believes the world is full of possibility that she personally will prove. Her speech is a wall of katakana English ('So good!', 'Amazing!', 'Fabulous!'), and she loves dancing, pantomime and grand gestures. Under the showmanship she is caring and sensible - she reminds the trainer about sunscreen, rest and hydration, and refuses back-to-back races because 'fighting on the world stage needs rest too'.

story_arc.summary: Pearl dreams of proving the world is full of possibility by racing abroad; her career is built around miles and sprints (Daily Hai Junior S, Hanshin JF, NHK Mile Cup, Mile CS, Takamatsunomiya Kinen, Yasuda Kinen, Sprinters S). Event titles show setbacks ('a little miscalculation' at the NHK Mile, an injury-like 'battered miracle' at the Mile CS, 'unerasable regret', a 'grounded airline') and memories of Paris, ending with 'Everyone is possible' after the Mile CS. Her real-horse namesake was the first Japan-trained horse to win a European Group 1 (Prix Maurice de Gheest, Deauville, 1998).
story_arc.source: event titles (trainee_event_titles); real-horse Deauville win is general knowledge (unverified), consistent with profile trivia 'ドーヴィルビーチ'
